beats.text: FlashAttention-2, an optimized attention algorithm, still achieved only 35% H100 GPU utilization. Why does attention remain such a bottleneck despite prior advancements?
beats.visual_focus: H100 GPU chip with '35% UTILIZED' overlay, showing a significant unused portion.

beats.text: The core problem is attention's heavy reliance on memory I/O. Constant movement of intermediate matrices between slow global memory and fast on-chip SRAM creates a severe data transfer bottleneck.
beats.visual_focus: Animated diagram showing data flowing between 'Global Memory (HBM)' and 'SRAM (Fast Cache)' with a large 'Data Transfer Bottleneck' label in between for Q, K, V matrices.

beats.text: FlashAttention-3 tackles this by exploiting Hopper H100 hardware: advanced asynchrony and native FP8 low-precision support. It cleverly overlaps computation with data movement via warp-specialization.
beats.visual_focus: Hopper H100 architecture schematic, highlighting 'Tensor Cores' and 'TMA (Transformer Memory Accelerator)' with arrows showing 'Asynchronous Operations' and 'FP8 Precision' labels.

beats.text: The mechanism involves interleaving block-wise matrix multiplications and softmax operations directly within SRAM, minimizing reads. Quantization to FP8 further shrinks data, enabling faster Tensor Core processing.
beats.visual_focus: Detailed animation: SRAM block showing iterative `Q_b K_b^T` followed by `softmax(S_b) V_b` operations within the same memory, then transitioning to an 'FP8 Block' for data reduction.

beats.text: This innovation yields significant gains: 1.5-2.0x speedup. FlashAttention-3 reaches 740 TFLOPs/s with FP16 and nearly 1.2 PFLOPs/s with FP8, pushing H100 utilization to 75%.
beats.visual_focus: Dynamic bar chart comparing 'FA-2' vs 'FA-3 (FP16)' vs 'FA-3 (FP8)' showing TFLOPs/s. Then a pie chart for H100 utilization with 75% highlighted.
